cards.sig: it’s got / gotten a lot greener. · it’s got / gotten a lot more built-up. green ↔ built-up more trees and parks · houses where there used to be fields
it’s got / gotten a lot busier. · it’s got / gotten a lot quieter / more quiet. busy ↔ quiet more people, more traffic · not as many cars
it’s got / gotten a lot more crowded. · it’s got / gotten a lot emptier. crowded ↔ empty you can’t move on saturdays · hardly anyone on the streets after six
it’s got / gotten a lot cleaner. · it’s got / gotten a lot dirtier. clean ↔ dirty clean streets now · trash on the streets
it’s got / gotten a lot safer. · it’s got / gotten a lot more dangerous. safe ↔ dangerous you can walk home at night · you don’t go out alone at night
it’s got / gotten a lot fancier. · it’s got / gotten a lot more run-down. fancy ↔ run-down cocktail bars instead of cheap cafés · peeling paint, broken windows
it’s got / gotten a lot pricier. · it’s got / gotten a lot more affordable. pricey ↔ affordable eight euros for a coffee! · rents have gone down
it’s got / gotten a lot livelier / more lively. lively new bars and cafés
it’s got / gotten a lot more touristy. touristy souvenir shops on every corner
it’s got / gotten a lot more modern. modern glass towers everywhere
it’s got / gotten a lot better. · it’s got / gotten a lot worse. good ↔ bad a new park, a new metro line · more crime, more traffic jams

the station has got / gotten a lot nicer. also fine: has become a lot nicer the station · nice they renovated it last year a place near you that has got / gotten a lot nicer — or a lot worse. what happened?

tvs are a lot cheaper than they used to be. also fine: tvs have got / gotten a lot cheaper. tvs · cheap you pay much less now than twenty years ago two things that are a lot cheaper — or a lot more expensive — than they used to be. which one do you notice most?
the summers are getting hotter and hotter. the summers · hot every year it’s worse two things that are getting better and better — or worse and worse — where you live. which one matters most to you?

my favourite restaurant isn’t as good as it used to be. also fine: … isn’t as good as it was. my favourite restaurant · good it was better ten years ago a café, a shop or a tv show that isn’t as good as it used to be. what’s changed?

the old town has become a lot more touristy. also fine: … is a lot more touristy than it used to be. the old town · touristy souvenir shops everywhere now a place that has become a lot more touristy — or one that hasn’t changed at all. why do you think that is?
my street is getting noisier and noisier. my street · noisy a new bar opens every month what’s getting more and more popular where you live? who’s happy about it, and who isn’t?
